formula_checks.name: isAlternative
formula_checks.why: An account is an alternative exactly when its class is Alternatives. The class comes from one rule (assetClassOf), so this agrees with the Alternatives line. A private-equity or hedge-fund row saved earlier stays an alternative, as owner rules 8 and 9 require.
formula_checks.rests_on: assetClassOf step order; owner rules 8 and 9 (2026-10-06, 2026-08-04).

formula_checks.name: valueFreshness
formula_checks.why: This is the standard whole-months-elapsed count. It handles the day-of-month boundary, the end-of-month case, a value dated by month only (counted from the 1st), a future date (never below zero) and the 'stale at 6 or more' line. An account built from its holdings has no hand-typed value to age, so no answer is right.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary calendar arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: portfolioActualReturn
formula_checks.why: The formula weights each account's reported twelve-month return by its earmarked balance TODAY, after that return has already happened. That overweights the account that grew most. Here is an example. $412,600 earmarked earned +18.4%, $96,250 earned -4.75% and $60,000 earned +11.2%. The formula gives +13.72%. The earmarked money grew from $503,486.43 to $568,850.00, which is +12.98%. The card's reason is that it must be 'weighted the same way as the plan's benchmark (blendedReturn)'. That does not hold: a forward-looking expected rate is rightly weighted by today's amounts, but a past return must be weighted by what was invested when the twelve months began. A today-weighted average is also not the time-weighted return that owner rule 1 requires for every return.
formula_checks.should_be: For each counted account, start value = earmarked balance ÷ (1 + reported return). Return = Σ earmarked balance ÷ Σ start value − 1. This is the same as averaging the reported returns weighted by start value. The other rules stay: property out, unreported returns left out (not read as 0), a reported 0 counted, accounts with nothing earmarked out, and no answer when the total is zero. Where money was added during the year, the reported return alone cannot recover the start value, so the screen should call the figure an estimate.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard performance-measurement practice: a portfolio's period return is the sum of its parts' returns weighted by their starting values (CFA Institute GIPS asset-weighting at beginning of period). Owner rule 1 (2026-10-04).

formula_checks.name: accountAllowsTicker
formula_checks.why: Bank, cash, property and 529 accounts cannot take ticker buys. An account that already lists holdings can. A single bond, CD or alternative typed by hand is itself one holding, so it cannot. Everything else (brokerage, 401(k), IRA, HSA, an unclassified typed account) can. The order is right: an account that already lists holdings is allowed before the class test.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary account practice: 529 plans hold plan portfolios, not exchange tickers.

formula_checks.name: assetKind
formula_checks.why: This is an exact-id lookup of app-written ids. Returning nothing for an id that is unknown, missing or spelled differently is the honest answer. It does not guess.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary lookup.

formula_checks.name: maturityClass
formula_checks.why: This follows the owner rule of 2026-08-04 (DEC-0051, DEC-0092): any instrument with a maturity date is Bonds & CDs, whatever its maturity. A blank date counts as none. Ignoring whether the date has passed is how the owner worded the rule ('regardless of how soon it matures').
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner rule 2026-08-04 (DEC-0051).

formula_checks.name: wrapperAccount
formula_checks.why: Each wrapper maps to the right kind and tax bucket. A Roth 401(k) is kind 401(k) in the Roth bucket, and an HSA is in the pre-tax bucket. When nothing is chosen, a plain taxable brokerage is the natural account, not an invented figure.
formula_checks.rests_on: IRS treatment of 401(k), IRA, Roth and HSA accounts.

formula_checks.name: assetClassOf
formula_checks.why: Step (1) takes 'the class stated on the account' first, but the type comment says the CSV importer as well as the person writes that field. The card does not separate a class the PERSON gave (MK-XS-I-048) from one an importer copied from a broker tag. A CD or a money-market fund that a broker tags 'cash' can then be imported with class cash and stay cash. That breaks the owner rule (DEC-0051/0092: cash means cash only; CDs are Bonds & CDs at any maturity; money-market funds are Stocks / Funds) and DEC-0309 ('name-first classification on every road, broker tag as fallback'). It also disagrees with MK-NW-F-109 holdingClassOf, which puts a holding's name evidence above the broker's tag. Name both cards.
formula_checks.should_be: (1) The class the person stated. (2) Bonds & CDs if it has a maturity date. (3) Name evidence. (4) A class written by an importer or broker, used only as a fallback. Then the remaining steps as now.

formula_checks.name: taxTreatmentOf
formula_checks.why: A stated treatment wins. Otherwise a 529 is tax-free, a pre-tax account (HSA included) is tax-deferred, a Roth account is tax-free and anything else is taxable. These match the IRS treatment of each wrapper.

formula_checks.name: taxWordsOf
formula_checks.why: The 529 and HSA wording is used only 'where no treatment is stated on the account'. Once a treatment is stated (the editor and importer both set it), a 529 stated tax-free reads 'tax-free (Roth)'. A 529 is not a Roth. An HSA stated tax-deferred reads 'pre-tax — taxed when it comes out', which is false for medical spending. No number changes, but the words on the account's page are false.
formula_checks.should_be: Check the kind first: a 529 always reads 'tax-free for education' and an HSA always reads 'pre-tax — tax-free for medical costs'. Only then use the treatment. 'Tax-free (Roth)' should be used only for an account in the Roth bucket; any other tax-free account reads 'tax-free'.
formula_checks.rests_on: IRC §529 and §223; ordinary consistency with MK-NW-F-012.

formula_checks.name: cashTotal
formula_checks.why: Cash = bank accounts whole, plus the uninvested cash inside linked and hand-built investment accounts. That is what the card says it is for, and it reproduces the approved drawing ($8,000 + $838 = $8,838). Money-market funds and CDs are not cash, per the owner rule. The fault that shows up next to it is in how the other lines handle hand-built accounts (see MK-NW-F-021).
formula_checks.rests_on: Approved drawing Net worth v08 state A; owner DEC-0051.

formula_checks.name: equitiesTotal
formula_checks.why: The card says 'an account holding several classes gives only its Stocks / Funds part', but the split it reads (assetAllocation, MK-NW-F-029) splits only a LINKED account. Every other account counts whole under its one class. A hand-built brokerage (derive_balance) with $6,120.55 of uninvested cash and $63,235.20 of VTI is counted whole, $69,355.75, under Stocks / Funds. The same $6,120.55 is also on the Cash line, because cashTotal (MK-NW-F-016) takes hand-built cash. A T-bill in a hand-built account lands in Stocks too, because MK-NW-F-027 leaves the rest of a hand-built account under its own class. The two cards disagree: cashTotal splits every account that has a class split, and assetAllocation splits only linked ones.
formula_checks.should_be: Stocks / Funds = for every account with a class split (linked OR hand-built), its Stocks / Funds part. The hand-built split must class each holding by holdingClassOf. Every other account counts whole.
formula_checks.rests_on: Card's own stated purpose; consistency with MK-NW-F-016 and MK-NW-F-027; owner DEC-0343 (a total and the sum of its parts are pinned by an invariant).

formula_checks.name: fixedIncomeTotal
formula_checks.why: The fault is the same as in MK-NW-F-017. A T-bill or CD held in a hand-built account is filed under the account's own class (Stocks / Funds) by MK-NW-F-027, and assetAllocation does not split hand-built accounts at all. That T-bill is then missing from Bonds & CDs, which breaks the owner rule that T-bills are Bonds & CDs (DEC-0051/0092). A hand-built account whose own class is Bonds & CDs would also put its uninvested cash in this line as well as in Cash.
formula_checks.should_be: Bonds & CDs = for every account with a class split (linked or hand-built), its Bonds & CDs part, with each holding classed by holdingClassOf. Every other account counts whole.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0051, DEC-0092; consistency with MK-NW-F-016/027/109.

formula_checks.name: alternativesTotal
formula_checks.why: The fault is the same as in MK-NW-F-017. A hand-built crypto account (own class Alternatives) with uninvested cash is counted whole as Alternatives. Its cash is also on the Cash line. The Other investments 'Total value' (MK-NW-M-049) then overstates by that cash.
formula_checks.should_be: Alternatives = for every account with a class split (linked or hand-built), its Alternatives part. Every other account counts whole.
formula_checks.rests_on: Consistency with MK-NW-F-016; owner DEC-0343.

formula_checks.name: realEstateTotal
formula_checks.why: Only property accounts can be Real estate: hand-built splits exclude property, and holdings are never classed Real estate by the rules on these cards. The Real estate line is therefore the whole value of every account classed Real estate, which is the right figure (gross, before any mortgage).
formula_checks.rests_on: assetClassOf step (4)/(7).

formula_checks.name: investmentsTotal
formula_checks.why: The card says 'Always: cashTotal + investmentsTotal = investableAssets'. That fails for a hand-built investment account with uninvested cash. cashTotal counts the cash. assetAllocation counts the whole account under its own class, so investmentsTotal counts the cash again. In the example, checking $5,000 plus a hand-built Schwab ($6,120.55 cash + $63,235.20 VTI) gives cash $11,120.55 and investments $69,355.75. Those add to $80,476.30, against investable assets of $74,355.75.
formula_checks.should_be: Investments = Stocks/Funds + Bonds & CDs + Alternatives + Unclassified, where every account with a class split (linked or hand-built) gives only its non-cash parts. Then cashTotal + investmentsTotal = investableAssets holds for every household.
formula_checks.rests_on: Card's own invariant; owner DEC-0343; consistency with MK-NW-F-016.

formula_checks.name: investableAssets
formula_checks.why: Investable assets = the balances of all accounts that are not real estate or personal property, each counted once. This matches what it is for. An overdrawn account counts at its negative balance.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: accountDisplayName
formula_checks.why: The card promises that 'a tax-advantaged account always shows what it is', but the kind word comes from the kind alone. A Roth 401(k) is kind 401(k) in the Roth bucket (MK-NW-F-010), so it reads 'Fidelity 401(k) -7712', the same as a pre-tax 401(k). A household with both at one employer cannot tell which is Roth. The tax-bucket override covers only a kind that says 'Brokerage'.
formula_checks.should_be: When the kind is 401(k) and the account is in the Roth bucket (or tax-free), the kind word is 'Roth 401(k)'.
formula_checks.rests_on: Card's own promise; MK-NW-F-010 mapping of roth_401k.

formula_checks.name: accountDisplayNames
formula_checks.why: Each account takes its own display name. Names that clash are numbered · 1, · 2 in the text order of their ids, which is creation order, and a number already used as another account's name is skipped. No two accounts can end up with the same name. Nothing here changes a number.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic; owner DEC-0382 (same words for the same thing).

formula_checks.name: holdingClassOf
formula_checks.why: Steps (1) to (3) are right and follow the owner's rules. Step (4) sends 'anything else' to Stocks / Funds, and that includes a holding with NO stored class at all. Such a holding has no name evidence and has not been marked as asked, so nothing says what kind of asset it is. The owner ruled for exactly that case: 'Refuse the line and ask' (2026-09-30). Stocks / Funds there is an invented default.
formula_checks.should_be: (4) bond → Bonds & CDs; other → Alternatives; cash → cash; a recognised equity or fund tag → Stocks / Funds. NO stored class and no evidence → Unclassified, and the holding is marked as asked.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner rule 7 (2026-09-30, master Q11).

formula_checks.name: accountClassBreakdown
formula_checks.why: The linked-account branch is right: cash, priced holdings by holdingClassOf, options in Alternatives, an unpriced remainder never put in cash, and the owner's $1/1% tolerance. The hand-built branch is not. It leaves 'the rest of the balance whole under the account's own class', so a hand-built account holding VTI and a US T-bill files the T-bill under Stocks / Funds. That breaks owner DEC-0051/0092, which makes T-bills Bonds & CDs. It also breaks the card's own goal of 'how much of one account sits in each class', and the promise of MK-NW-F-109 and MK-NW-F-028 that the split, the words and the page all use one rule. A hand-built account's balance is cash plus Σ(shares × price), so its holdings can be split exactly.
formula_checks.should_be: Hand-built account: cash = recorded uninvested cash, capped at the balance. Each holding = shares × price under holdingClassOf. Any remainder is handled as for a linked account. The parts still add to the balance.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0051, DEC-0092; MK-NW-F-109 'the one rule the split, the words under it and the account's page all use'.

formula_checks.name: classPortionLabel
formula_checks.why: The counting is right. It uses the same class test as the dollars (holdingClassOf). It names CDs and Treasuries as the owner asked (DEC-0090), drops zero counts and joins parts with '&' and 'A, B & C'. 'CDW Corp' rightly does not count as a CD. Two gaps change the words a person reads. (1) A Treasury described the way a broker sends it ('UNITED STATES TREAS BILLS 0% 01/15/27', 'US TREAS NT') has none of the whole words Treasury, T-bill, T-note or government, so it is counted as a bond. The words then read '1 CD & 1 bond' for an account holding a CD and a T-bill. (2) The plural of Treasury is not given ('2 Treasuries' or '2 Treasurys').
formula_checks.should_be: Count as Treasury any holding whose name has Treasury, Treas, UST, T-bill, T-bills, Bill(s) with a US Treasury issuer, T-note or T-bond (capitals ignored, whole words). Plurals: CDs, Treasuries, bonds.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0090 (2026-08-11); ordinary broker description formats.

formula_checks.name: theNetWorth
formula_checks.why: (a) Investments double-count the uninvested cash of a hand-built account (see MK-NW-F-021). The card promises 'Cash + Investments + property comes to everything owned', but for a hand-built account it adds to more than Assets. The same wrong number reaches /home and /analytics (YOUR INVESTMENTS) and /insights (Total invested), so all three agree with each other and are all wrong. (b) Debts: each line uses 'the larger of the minimum and the payment set', but the card does not say which monthly total is printed as 'Monthly debt payments' (MK-NW-M-012) on /analytics and /home. That figure answers 'what all your debts REQUIRE', which is the minimum, while the type comment says the screen prints the minimum and the line rule prints the larger. The card is also silent on a debt whose minimum was never entered (M-011 refuses) as against one that genuinely requires $0. (c) The return is correctly time-weighted (owner rule 1), but the card does not say that a recorded day's value is taken AFTER that day's money moved. MK-NW-O-008 says so, and the rule is needed to work out 'the value just before the next movement'. Name both cards. (d) With nothing entered, the formula adds nothing up and gives Net worth $0, Cash $0 and Investments $0. The TheNetWorth type has no empty value, yet MK-XS-M-001 must say 'Nothing entered yet' rather than 'showing $0 as a fact'. The card does not say how the orchestrator tells 'nothing entered' from a real $0. The approved drawing reproduces exactly, provided the Vanguard account is linked.
formula_checks.should_be: Investments = the non-cash parts of every account with a class split (linked or hand-built) + every other investment account whole, so Cash + Investments + Real estate + Personal property = Assets. Monthly debt payments: state which total the screen prints. A debt with no minimum entered is refused on its line and named in the total's footnote, never added as $0. Return: say that a recorded day's value is taken after that day's money moved, the same way as MK-NW-O-008. With no accounts and no debts, hand back 'nothing entered' (null figures), never $0.
formula_checks.rests_on: Card's own invariant; owner DEC-0343; owner rule 1 (2026-10-04); approved drawing Net worth v08 state A.

formula_checks.name: thePerformance
formula_checks.why: (a) When the record cannot reach the beginning, the formula BACK-SOLVES one: beginning = ending − priced gain − contributions + withdrawals. Wealth generated then equals the priced gain. Both are shown as if they were measured. That contradicts what the card's own figures say they must do. Wealth generated (MK-PF-M-002) refuses: 'nothing honest to subtract from'. Beginning market value (MK-PF-M-013) says 'the walk is not drawn at all rather than started from a guess'. It also contradicts owner DEC-0230 ('We never back-fill …'). It is the 'invented default where the honest answer is no answer' shape. (b) Read literally, the beginning is read 'at the day BEFORE the period opens', and only when the record's first day is on or before that day. A Since window opens on the record's first day, so every Since figure would refuse. The type (WindowFigures.beginningAsOf) says Since reads the record's first day, so the card is silent on its own most-used window. (c) It does not say which day the yearly-rate test counts days from: the window's first day or the beginning day (the day before). For a window that opens exactly two years ago, the yearly rate is +10.00% counted one way and +10.01% the other. The TWR pieces themselves, the walk and the ending are right, and they reproduce the approved drawing.
formula_checks.should_be: When the record cannot reach the window's beginning: no beginning and no wealth generated. Either the walk is not drawn, or it starts on the record's first day and says so. No percent either way, and never a back-solved start. For Since: the beginning is the record's first recorded day. Years = days from the window's first day to today ÷ 365. A window of exactly one year (365 days) is then shown as its total, and exactly two years (730 days) gives years = 2. The card should say this.
formula_checks.rests_on: MK-PF-M-002/013/018 refusal rules; owner DEC-0230; owner rule 1 (2026-10-04); approved drawing Performance v17 phone 1.
